source.author: cic
source.text: Brutus, quem ego honoris causa nomino, cruentum pugionem tenens Ciceronem exclamavit: ex quo intellegi debet eum conscium fuisse.
source.text_original: 'Brutus, quem ego honoris causa nomino, cruentum pugionem tenens Ciceronem exclamavit: ex quo intellegi debet eum conscium fuisse.'
source.text_english: Brutus, whom I name out of respect, holding the bloody dagger, cried out, “Cicero!” From this it must be understood that he was aware of it.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: pater tuus, quem ego honoris causa nomino non quia consularis et patricius, sed quia Christianus est , inpleat nomen suum et laetetur filiam Christo se genuisse, non saeculo; quin potius doleat, quod et uirginitatem frustra amiseris et fructus perdideris nuptiarum.
reuse.text_original: pater tuus, quem ego honoris causa nomino — non quia consularis et patricius, sed quia Christianus est —, inpleat nomen suum et laetetur filiam Christo se genuisse, non saeculo; quin potius doleat, quod et uirginitatem frustra amiseris et fructus perdideris nuptiarum.
reuse.text_english: May your father, whom I name out of respect, not because he is a man of consular rank and a patrician, but because he is a Christian, live up to his name and rejoice that he has begotten a daughter for Christ, not for the world; rather, let him grieve that you have lost your virginity in vain and have lost the fruit of marriage as well.
